name: strops-find
algorithm: Find every non-overlapping occurrence of 8 fixed needles (3 to 16 bytes) in each line of a 50 MB text with each language's std substring search; add each match's offset in its line plus 1, wrapping; rounds times (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; a search has no arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries, each with its own search algorithm; every library returns the first match at or after p, so the sum of the offsets checks every result
notes: Searches named: mk str.Find; c strstr over NUL-terminated lines (labelled: each newline of the buffer is overwritten with NUL once, before the rounds, since strstr needs C strings); rust str::find (Two-Way); zig std.mem.findPos; go strings.Index; cs ReadOnlySpan<char>.IndexOf(StringComparison.Ordinal). Lines: mk str.Lines, rust str::lines, zig std.mem.splitScalar, go strings.SplitSeq, cs MemoryExtensions.Split; c walks the NULs.
The input is wordfreq's file (the same data spec, so one generated file serves both rows).
